record.tranche_reason: It compares learned feature representations using interpretability ratings and reconstruction error, providing a different-measure test of indirect evidence from dictionary features in a transformer MLP.
record.gate_note: The post reports comparisons of distilled-model feature groups with an autoencoder, including interpretability scores and reconstruction errors. Figure 5 describes ablation and L1-sweep outcomes, but most plotted values are not available in the supplied text, so they are not recorded as numeric rows. The comments are by other authors and are not treated as results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study bears on V4 only weakly. The author-rated interpretability of sparse dictionary-like features (from the SAE and from sparse distillation) is far higher than that of neuron-like units. The author says those neuron-like units are no better than the original polysemantic neurons. Most of the post compares the author's distillation method with an SAE, which is method performance, not a test of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. Sparse distillation was worse than the autoencoder on reconstruction error and monosemanticity, and focusing on a single MLP may miss multi-layer features.
record.recipe_differences: This is a sparse MLP distillation study compared with an autoencoder, not a reproduction of the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports that GELU yields 70% neuron simulators and that its remaining sparse features are almost dead; the ReLU and GELU conditions therefore differ. The L1 sweep also changes reconstruction and the number of dead neurons, though most plotted values are not available in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: About 29% of the distilled MLP's neurons become 'neuron simulators' that copy original neurons, with decoder cosine above 0.8. Mean-ablation shows these do most of the reconstruction work. With GELU, 70% are simulators.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse distillation of an MLP partly reproduces the original polysemantic neurons instead of decomposing them into sparse features.

record.problems: The author scored top-activating examples with a rubric, but the post does not report uncertainty or agreement for those ratings. Only the first 50 neurons of each model were inspected. Most Figure 5 values are not available in the supplied text. The experiments described are focused on a single transformer and its MLPs.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 5 contains additional reconstruction-error and dead-neuron results across L1 settings and feature-type ablations, but the supplied text gives no exact values for most plotted points. Appendix C describes layer 0 distributions as similar and shows figures without numerical outcomes; those results do not directly measure V4's autoencoder-feature claim.

untested.parts: Only one tiny model (TinyStories-2L-33M, second MLP) was studied. There is no test of features spread across neurons beyond the decoder-similarity analysis, and no check across LLMs.
The study does not test completeness, stability, or canonicity of SAE features. It only notes conceptually that features may span multiple MLPs.

missing.what: Qualitative ablation result: sparse features alone leave most of the MLP's function unexplained, and higher L1 penalties kill neurons. This bears on how much of the MLP the sparse features account for.

record.verdict_notes: The record's labels treated the method-comparison rows (r4, r5) as evidence for V4. I have unlinked them. The limits_scope label in the record concerned the distillation method, not V4, so I dropped it. The comments are by other people and are not results of this study.

versions.untested_parts: No test of toy-model superposition, overlap geometry, or a sparsity-dependent geometric transition.
The study does not test whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
The study does not establish that polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.

Tests autoencoder features on one transformer MLP and a limited sample of features; it does not establish how widespread these results are across LLMs or test features spread across neurons in the original model.
No test of whether autoencoder features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No test comparing one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.
